note: The input begins with the MZ signature, causing the MS-DOS/PE magic subtree to be evaluated on candidate-controlled bytes.
The candidate-controlled little-endian value at file offset 0x3c is used as an indirect offset to locate the PE signature.
The PE subsystem rule requires a two-byte leshort at e_lfanew+92, but the tiny truncated optional header supplies only the low subsystem byte before the file ends.
The computed PE-field offset reaches the end of the candidate buffer, so the implementation copies the remaining candidate byte for a two-byte magic value and relies on padding for the missing byte.
